chunks: 3220 - Hariz narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام that he said:

“Any man who has a dispute with his brother over a right, and he calls him to a man from among your brothers to judge between him and him, but he refuses and insists on taking him to these, is like those about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:”

“Have you not seen those who claim that they have believed in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you? They wish to seek judgment from Taghut, though they were commanded to reject it.”

key_terms.الطَّاغُوتِ: a false or illegitimate authority whose judgment is not to be sought
key_terms.حَقٍّ: a due right or rightful claim under dispute
key_terms.لِيَحْكُمَ: to judge or arbitrate between disputing parties
key_terms.مُمَارَاةٌ: a dispute or contention between two parties
key_terms.يَكْفُرُوا بِهِ: to reject and disavow that false authority
key_terms.يُرَافِعَهُ: to bring him before an authority for judgment

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about taking disputes to unjust judges instead of a believer?
ai.summary: This hadith condemns referring disputes over rights to illegitimate authorities when a just believer is available to judge between the parties. It applies the Quranic censure of seeking judgment from al-Taghut to those who knowingly reject rightful adjudication and turn instead to unjust judges.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3220 - Hariz narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (as) that he said:

"Any man who has a dispute with his brother over a right, and he calls him to a man from among your brothers to judge between them, but he refuses and insists on taking him to these (unjust judges), is like those about whom Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, said:
'Have you not seen those who claim to have believed in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you? They wish to refer their judgment to Taghut, while they were commanded to reject it'"
